newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds reverse direction to close stronger.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds reverse direction to close stronger.

text.p: Canadian bonds pared early losses to close higher on Wednesday, rallying in tandem with U.S. Treasuries, which closed stronger amid optimism about a U.S. balanced budget agreement, analysts said.

"The market came back, I think it had to do with optimism over a U.S. budget deal. There is a lot of talk about that," said Harvinder Kalirai, Canadian analyst with New York-based financial analysis firm I.D.E.A.
Canada's 30-year benchmark rose C$0.62 to C$109.90 to yield 7.156 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond rose 13/32 to yield 6.95 percent.
The spread between the two bonds narrowed to 21 basis points on Wednesday from 23 basis points at the close of trading on Tuesday.

Both Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets opened weaker on Wednesday following a report that U.S. GDP grew at an annual rate of 5.6 percent in the first quarter. A Reuters survey of economists had expected, on average, a 4.1 percent rise in the first quarter.
However, Canadian bonds reversed direction with U.S. Treasuries after a U.S. politician suggested a budget pact may be in sight.
In Canada, an economic report showed monthly GDP data rose 0.5 percent in February. The increase was in line with expectations and had little impact on markets.

"The Canadian data didn't really push the market in Canada. You are seeing strong growth in Canada, but the Bank of Canada has made it quite clear that there is such a wide output gap that the economy could grow for several quarters without any inflation," said Kalirai.
Among new issues, the Bank of Canada on Thursday will release details of the federal government's auction of 10-year bonds on May 7.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bonds rose C$0.32 to C$102.60 to yield 6.627 percent. The U.S. bond rose 10/32 to yield 6.72 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to nine basis points from eight basis points at Tuesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.15 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.25 percent.
